model: claude-sonnet-5 (via general-purpose subagent, one independent session per language)

vibe.notes: No compile-error iterations needed on the final attempt (some earlier research iterations while discovering the Fs/Env/Stderr host-effect API, which is not documented in docs/cheatsheet.md -- had to read lib/@vibe/shell/commands.vibe, lib/@vibe/io/io.vibe, and fixtures/runtime/*.vibe directly). Hand-rolled filter/sort instead of importing lib/@vibe/prelude helpers (import-path uncertainty from a deeply nested eval/ directory). Used a dedicated char-code string comparator to avoid the known String `<` pointer-order (not lexicographic) pitfall documented in lib/@vibe/prelude/cmp.vibe.

rust.notes: Zero external crates, stdlib only. No real friction; ~12s release build. Storage: three flat line-based files under .mvcs/ (staged, tracked, commits).

typescript.notes: No build step used -- ran directly via `node --experimental-strip-types src/minivcs.ts` (Node 22 native TS stripping). No standalone binary, so artifact_bytes is not applicable (see eval/lang-bench/langs/typescript/README.md). Storage: four small JSON files under .mvcs/.

gleam.notes: not run (no toolchain in this sandbox, 2026-07-22)

moonbit.notes: not run (no toolchain in this sandbox, 2026-07-22)

verification: All three pass counts independently re-verified by running eval/lang-bench/acceptance_test.sh against each built artifact after the fact (not just trusting each implementer agent's self-report).
summary: All 3 implementable languages here hit 12/12 acceptance on the first delivered attempt. vibe's wasm artifact (19.5 KB) is far smaller than rust's stripped native binary (322 KB) for the same program -- expected given wasm vs a statically-linked native binary with a runtime, not a controlled apples-to-apples size comparison. vibe needed the most LOC (309 vs rust 182 / ts 178), largely from hand-rolling Array::filter/sort (not vibe builtins) and from more verbose host-effect plumbing (Fs/Env/Stderr) than Rust's std or Node's fs/process -- see docs/pl-survey-2026-07.md's structured-diagnostics priority item and eval/msr findings for related stdlib-discoverability friction.
